title: Ratatouille
subtitle: Provençal stewed summer vegetables with tomatoes and herbs
excerpt: A slow-cooked stew of aubergine, courgette, peppers, and tomatoes from Provence, fragrant with garlic, basil, and thyme. Equally good warm as a side dish or cold the next day with bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ratatouille is a Provençal dish from Nice. The name derives from the verb touiller, to stir or toss. The classic method calls for cooking each vegetable separately before combining them, which preserves their individual textures and flavours. Many modern versions cook everything together, which is quicker but produces a more uniform, softer result. The dish is at its best in late summer when all the vegetables are in season at the same time. It is traditionally served as a side dish but is also eaten as a main with bread, or cold as a room-temperature salad.

recipeTools.notes: Wide and heavy-based for even cooking.

content.text: For the best texture, fry the aubergine and courgette separately before adding them to the tomato base. This keeps each vegetable distinct rather than turning the stew into a uniform mush. Salt the aubergine for 20 minutes before cooking to draw out bitterness and excess moisture; this also means it absorbs less oil. The dish improves the day after it is made: cook it ahead and reheat gently.

Salt the aubergine cubes and leave for 20 minutes. Pat dry. Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Fry the aubergine in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until golden. Remove from the pan and set aside. Add another tablespoon of oil and fry the courgette for 4 minutes until lightly coloured. Set aside.

Add the remaining oil to the pan. Cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add the peppers and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato puree, thyme, and bay leaves. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and season. Simmer for 10 minutes.

Add the aubergine and courgette back to the pan. Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until all the vegetables are tender and the sauce has thickened. Remove the herb sprigs. Tear the basil over the top. Serve warm or at room temperature.
